original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-nil}
Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $A$ be a ring, let $I \subset A$ be an ideal,
and let $\gamma$ be a divided power structure on $I$. Assume $p$ is nilpotent
in $A/I$. Then $I$ is locally nilpotent if and only if $p$ is nilpotent in $A$.

semantic_review_note: For a PD ideal (I,γ) in A and prime p nilpotent mod I, I is locally nilpotent precisely when p is nilpotent in A. Both directions and the preliminary p-in-A/I nilpotence hypothesis are retained.
